extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, patent examiners, and legal practitioners/students working with U.S. patent and related antitrust statutes
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory and procedural standards governing enforcement of antitrust orders, injunctions and contempt procedures, Patent Office organization and personnel, wartime extensions for patent/trademark filings, and index pointers to patent-law doctrines (abandonment, applications, assignments, appeals, etc.). Useful for practitioners evaluating compliance, remedies, and procedural posture in patent and related cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission/board power to modify orders pre-appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Until a transcript of the record in such hearing shall have been filed in a circuit court of appeals ... the commission or board may at any time, upon such notice and in such manner as it shall deem proper, modify or set aside, in whole or in part, any report or any order made or issued by it under this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission may revisit/alter its orders while administrative review in circuit court has not been brought to filing; no specific limits stated other than giving notice and manner it deems proper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement by filing transcript to circuit court
rubrics_metrics.description: If such person fails or neglects to obey such order ... the commission or board may apply to the circuit court of appeals ... and shall certify and file with its application a transcript of the entire record in the proceeding, including all the testimony taken and the report and order of the commission or board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforcement requires filing the full administrative record (testimony, report, order) in the appropriate circuit court of appeals (where violation committed or where person resides or does business).

rubrics_metrics.name: Court review scope and deference to administrative findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon such filing ... the court shall ... have power to make and enter upon the pleadings, testimony, and proceedings set forth in such transcript a decree affirming, modifying, or setting aside the order of the commission or board. The findings of the commission or board as to the facts, if supported by testimony, shall be conclusive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts review the administrative record and may affirm/modify/set aside; factual findings supported by testimony are conclusive (high deference).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for adducing additional evidence on court review
rubrics_metrics.description: If either party shall apply to the court for leave to adduce additional evidence, and shall show ... that such additional evidence is material and that there were reasonable grounds for the failure to adduce such evidence in the proceeding before the commission or board, the court may order such additional evidence to be taken before the commission or board and to be adduced upon the hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court can remand to administrative body to receive new evidence if material and reasonable excuse shown; commission may then modify findings and file modified/new findings with return of additional evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of party to seek review by circuit court of appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party required by such order of the commission or board to cease and desist from a violation charged may obtain a review of such order in said circuit court of appeals by filing in the court a written petition praying that the order of the commission or board be set aside. ... the commission or board forthwith shall certify and file in the court a transcript of the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggrieved parties may initiate review in the circuit court of appeals by petition and the commission must file the record; court has same jurisdiction as for enforcement applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusivity and expedition of circuit-court jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: The jurisdiction of the circuit court of appeals of the United States to enforce, set aside, or modify orders of the commission or board shall be exclusive. Such proceedings ... shall be given precedence over other cases pending therein, and shall be in every way expedited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Circuit court review/enforcement proceedings are exclusive and entitled to priority handling/expedited treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orders do not relieve other antitrust liability
rubrics_metrics.description: No order of the commission or board or the judgment of the court to enforce the same shall in any wise relieve or absolve any person from any liability under the antitrust Acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative/court enforcement does not immunize a party from other antitrust liabilities or separate prosecutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods of service of commission/board complaints and orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaints, orders, and other processes of the commission or board ... may be served ... (a) by delivering a copy thereof to the person to be served, or to a member of the partnership ... or to the president, secretary, or other executive officer or a director of the corporation to be served; or (b) by leaving a copy thereof at the principal office or place of business of such person; or (c) by registering and mailing a copy thereof addressed to such person at his principal office or place of business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service may be personal delivery, leaving at principal office, or registered mailing; verified return of server or registered-mail receipt are proof of service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Venue for antitrust suits against corporations
rubrics_metrics.description: Any suit, action, or proceeding under the antitrust laws against a corporation may be brought not only in the judicial district whereof it is an inhabitant, but also in any district wherein it may be found or transacts business; and all process ... may be served in the district of which it is an inhabitant, or wherever it may be found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flexible venue: suits may be brought where corporation is an inhabitant, found, or transacts business; process may be served where found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpoena reach and 100-mile civil witness limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpoenas for witnesses who are required to attend a court ... may run into any other district: Provided, That in civil cases no writ of subpoena shall issue for witnesses living out of the district ... at a greater distance than one hundred miles ... without the permission of the trial court being first had upon proper application and cause shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feds may subpoena witnesses nationwide, but in civil cases travel beyond 100 miles requires court permission on cause shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate officer/director criminal liability for corporate violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever a corporation shall violate any of the penal provisions of the antitrust laws, such violation shall be deemed to be also that of the individual directors, officers, or agents ... who shall have authorized, ordered, or done any of the acts constituting ... such violation, and such violation shall be deemed a misdemeanor, and upon conviction ... he shall be punished by a fine of not exceeding $5,000 or by imprisonment for not exceeding one year, or by both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directors/officers/agents who authorized/ordered/did offending acts are criminally liable as misdemeanants with defined maximum penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: District-court equitable jurisdiction to enjoin antitrust violations
rubrics_metrics.description: The several district courts of the United States are hereby invested with jurisdiction to prevent and restrain violations of this Act, and it shall be the duty of the several district attorneys ... to institute proceedings in equity to prevent and restrain such violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal district courts can issue equitable relief to prevent/restrain antitrust violations; U.S. district attorneys under AG direction must institute such proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for temporary restraining orders and additional parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Such proceedings may be by way of petition ... When the parties complained of shall have been duly notified ... the court shall proceed, as soon as may be, to the hearing ... pending such petition, and before final decree, the court may at any time make such temporary restraining order or prohibition as shall be deemed just ... Whenever it shall appear ... that the ends of justice require that other parties should be brought before the court, the court may cause them to be summoned, whether they reside in the district ... and subpoenas to that end may be served in any district by the marshal thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts may issue TROs pending hearing and may bring in additional parties by summons/subpoena across districts when justice requires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of private parties to seek injunctive relief (with exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person, firm, corporation, or association shall be entitled to sue for and have injunctive relief ... against threatened loss or damage by a violation of the antitrust laws ... and upon the execution of proper bond ... and a showing that the danger of irreparable loss or damage is immediate, a preliminary injunction may issue: Provided, That nothing therein contained shall be construed to entitle any person ... except the United States, to bring suit in equity ... against any common carrier ... in respect of any matter subject to the regulation ... of the Interstate Commerce Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private parties may seek injunctions for threatened antitrust harm under ordinary equitable principles and bond requirement, but may not (except U.S.) bring equity suits against ICC-regulated common-carrier matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requirement for preliminary injunctions
rubrics_metrics.description: That no preliminary injunction shall be issued without notice to the opposite party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary injunctions require notice to the adverse party (no ex parte preliminary injunctions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary restraining order (TRO) no-notice exception and contents
rubrics_metrics.description: No temporary restraining order shall be granted without notice ... unless it shall clearly appear from specific facts shown by affidavit or by the verified bill that immediate and irreparable injury, loss, or damage will result ... Every such temporary restraining order shall be indorsed with the date and hour of issuance, shall be forthwith filed in the clerk's office and entered of record, shall define the injury and state why it is irreparable and why the order was granted without notice, and shall ... expire within such time after entry, not to exceed ten days, as the court or judge may fix, unless ... extended ... for good cause shown, and the reasons for such extension shall be entered of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict formal requirements for ex parte TROs: affidavit/verified bill showing immediacy/irreparability, recordation of issuance time, statement of irreparable injury and reason for no notice, ten-day max duration unless extended with entered reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to proceed to preliminary injunction hearing after TRO
rubrics_metrics.description: In case a temporary restraining order shall be granted without notice in the contingency specified, the matter of the issuance of a preliminary injunction shall be set down for a hearing at the earliest possible time and shall take precedence ... and when the same comes up for hearing the party obtaining the temporary restraining order shall proceed with the application for a preliminary injunction, and if he does not do so the court shall dissolve the temporary restraining order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If TRO issued without notice, the movant must promptly seek preliminary injunction at earliest hearing; failure to do so leads to dissolution of TRO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposing party's right to move dissolution/modification of TRO
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon two days' notice to the party obtaining such temporary restraining order the opposite party may appear and move the dissolution or modification of the order, and in that event the court or judge shall proceed to hear and determine the motion as expeditiously as the ends of justice may require.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opposing party may seek prompt relief against TRO on short notice; court obliged to hear expeditiously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement of security for restraining/interlocutory injunctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as otherwise provided in section sixteen of this Act, no restraining order or interlocutory order of injunction shall issue, except upon the giving of security by the applicant in such sum as the court or judge may deem proper, conditioned upon the payment of such costs and damages as may be incurred or suffered by any party who may be found to have been wrongfully enjoined or restrained thereby.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts generally require bond/security from applicants for injunctions to cover costs/damages if injunction later found wrongful; section 16 (private antitrust suits) provides a specific proviso.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity and scope limits of injunction orders
rubrics_metrics.description: That every order of injunction or restraining order shall set forth the reasons for the issuance of the same, shall be specific in terms, and shall describe in reasonable detail, and not by reference to the bill of complaint or other document, the act or acts sought to be restrained, and shall be binding only upon the parties to the suit, their officers, agents, servants, employees and attorneys, or those in active concert or participating with them, and who shall, by personal service, or otherwise, have received actual notice of the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Injunctions must state reasons, be specific, describe acts restrained in reasonable detail (no mere incorporation by reference), and bind only named parties and those given actual notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contempt for willful disobedience of court orders
rubrics_metrics.description: That any person who shall willfully disobey any lawful writ, process, order, rule, decree or command of any district court ... by doing any act or thing therein, or thereby forbidden to be done by him ... shall be proceeded against for his said contempt as hereinafter provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Willful disobedience of court orders is contempt and triggers statutory contempt procedures and penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contempt charging and process (rule to show cause; attachment; bail)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever it shall be made to appear ... that there is reasonable ground to believe that any person has been guilty of such contempt, the court ... may issue a rule requiring the said person ... to show cause ... which rule, together with a copy of the affidavit or information, shall be served ... If ... the alleged contempt be not sufficiently purged, a trial shall be directed ... if the accused, being a natural person, fail or refuse to make return to the rule to show cause, an attachment may issue against his person ... he may be required to give reasonable bail for his attendance ... Where the accused is a body corporate, an attachment for the sequestration of its property may be issued ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory sequence: rule to show cause based on officer return/affidavit/DA info; service; trial if not purged; attachments and bail for nonappearance; sequestration attachments for corporations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to jury trial and criminal-like procedures for contempt
rubrics_metrics.description: In all cases within the purview of this Act such trial may be by the court, or, upon demand of the accused, by a jury; ... such trial shall conform as near as may be to the practice in criminal cases prosecuted by indictment or upon information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contempt trials can be jury trials on demand and generally follow criminal practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum contempt penalties (statutory limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the accused be found guilty, judgment shall be entered accordingly, prescribing the punishment, either by fine or imprisonment, or both, ... such fine shall be paid to the United States, or to the complainant ... but in no case shall the fine to be paid to the United States exceed, in case the accused is a natural person, the sum of $1,000, nor shall such imprisonment exceed the term of six months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory caps for fines ($1,000 to US) and imprisonment (6 months) for contempt convictions of natural persons, with possibilities of fines paid to injured parties and apportionment among multiple injured parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contempt proceedings time limitation and non-exclusivity with criminal prosecutions
rubrics_metrics.description: That no proceeding for contempt shall be instituted against any person unless begun within one year from the date of the act complained of; nor shall any such proceeding be a bar to any criminal prosecution for the same act or acts ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One-year statute of limitations for contempt proceedings; contempt proceeding does not bar subsequent criminal prosecution for same act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severability clause for the Act's provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: That if any clause, sentence, paragraph, or part of this Act shall ... be adjudged ... to be invalid, such judgment shall not affect, impair, or invalidate the remainder thereof, but shall be confined in its operation to the clause, sentence, paragraph, or part thereof directly involved ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard severability: invalidity of part does not void remainder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Office staffing and examiner grades (Patent Act of 1916)
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be in the Patent Office: One chief clerk, who shall be qualified to act as a principal examiner. One librarian, who shall be qualified to act as an assistant examiner. Five law examiners. One examiner of classification. One examiner of interferences. One examiner of trade-marks and designs. One first assistant examiner of trade-marks and designs. Six assistant examiners of trade-marks and designs. Forty-three principal examiners. Eighty-six first assistant examiners. Eighty-six second assistant examiners. Eighty-six third assistant examiners. Eighty-six fourth assistant examiners; and such other examiners and assistant examiners in the various grades as the Congress shall from time to time provide for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory specification of office positions and examiner staffing levels and roles (as of 1916 Act).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Office officers appointment and duties
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be in the Patent Office a Commissioner of Patents, one first assistant commissioner, one assistant commissioner, and five examiners in chief, who shall be appointed by the President, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate. The first assistant commissioner and the assistant commissioner shall perform such duties ... as may be assigned to them ... All other officers, clerks, and employees authorized by law for the office shall be appointed by the Secretary of the Interior upon the nomination of the Commissioner of Patents, in accordance with existing law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies appointment method for senior Patent Office officials (Presidential appointment with Senate advice/consent) and supervisory assignment of duties; other staff appointed by Secretary upon Commissioner's nomination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Office statutory salaries (specified amounts)
rubrics_metrics.description: The salaries of the officers mentioned in the preceding section shall be as follows: The Commissioner of Patents, $5,000 a year. The first Assistant Commissioner of Patents, $4,500 a year. The Assistant Commissioner of Patents, $3,500 a year. Five examiners in chief, $3,500 a year each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory salary schedule for chief Patent Office officers (historical figures as set by Act).

rubrics_metrics.name: Wartime extension of filing deadlines (Aug 17, 1916 Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any applicant for letters patent or for the registration of any trade-mark, print, or label, ... if unable on account of the existing and continuing state of war to file any application or pay any official fee or take any required action within the period now limited by law, shall be granted an extension of nine months beyond the expiration of said period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automatic 9-month extension for filing fees/actions where inability attributable to state of war; applies to patents and certain registrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for wartime extension (reciprocity and hostile-state exception)
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of this Act shall be limited to citizens or subjects of countries which extend substantially similar privileges to the citizens of the United States, and no extension shall be granted under this Act to the citizens or subjects of any country while said country is at war with the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility conditioned on reciprocity (foreign countries granting similar privileges) and excludes citizens/subjects of countries at war with the U.S.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and retroactivity of wartime-default relief
rubrics_metrics.description: This Act shall be operative to relieve from default under existing law occurring since August first, nineteen hundred and fourteen, and before the first day of January, nineteen hundred and eighteen, and all applications and letters patent and registrations in the filing or prosecution whereof default has occurred for which this Act grants relief shall have the same force and effect as if said default had not occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Act operates to relieve applicants from defaults occurring in specified war period and treats affected applications/patents/registrations as if default had not occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment doctrines (actual and constructive) — index synopsis
rubrics_metrics.description: Abandonment: actual, of applications; actual of invention; actual by acquiescence in rejection of application; actual by declaration; actual by delay; actual by disclaimer; actual by laches; burden of proof of actual abandonment; constructive abandonment of applications; constructive of applications by failing to bring suit to compel issuance; constructive of application, working constructive abandonment of invention; constructive of invention must be negatived in declarations and bills; constructive not condoned by excuses; degree of proof required; evidence of actual/constructive abandonment; several kinds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index summarizes multiple forms of abandonment (actual vs constructive), evidentiary burdens, and procedural implications (how pleaded, effect on rights). Use treatise sections cited for detailed rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications: elements, amendments, examination, dates, evidence — index items
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications: actual abandonment of, amendments of, assignment of without request that patent issue to assignee (effect), Commissioner's decisions upon, constructive abandonment of, dates of applications and how proven, elements of applications, equivalent to reduction to practice, examination of, fees due upon filing, formalities of execution, may fix dates of inventions, never negative novelty, not a part of the prior art, re-examination of, rejection of, renewal of abandoned, withdrawal of.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index indicates numerous statutory/doctrinal standards about patent applications: formalities, evidentiary weight, amendment and abandonment rules, fee obligations, and examination/reexamination procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignments: writing requirement and recording — index items
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignments: authenticated, how; conflicting; consideration for; construction of; defined; descriptions in; equitable; how proved; must be in writing; notice of; of extensions; of inventions; of licenses; of patents; recording of; reformation of; State laws imposing restrictions on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summary of assignment-related legal standards: statutory/formal requirements (writing), proof, recording, conflicts, and interplay with state law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals from Patent Office and courts — index items
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals: from examiners to board of examiners-in-chief; from board of examiners-in-chief to Commissioner of Patents; from Commissioner to Court of Appeals of D.C.; from Court of Appeals of D.C. to Supreme Court of the U.S.; from District Courts to Circuit Courts of Appeals; order for preliminary injunction not usually reviewed unless abuse of discretion appears.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index notes the administrative and judicial appeal routes and standards (e.g., limited review of interlocutory injunction orders absent abuse).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bills in equity and preliminary injunctions in patent practice — index items
rubrics_metrics.description: Bills in Equity: amendments of, answers to, defences to, for preliminary injunctions, interrogating part, introductory part, may be based on fear of future infringement, need not specify part of defendant's device alleged to infringe, oaths to, original, may be composite, may be used to perpetuate testimony, verified, when must specify claims alleged to be infringed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treatise index points to procedural/formal standards for equitable pleadings in patent suits (what to allege, verification, pleading claims, preliminary injunction practice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bonds and security in patent injunction proceedings — index items
rubrics_metrics.description: Bonds: as alternative to permanent injunctions where patent has short time to run; required from complainants on issuing preliminary injunctions; required from defendants in place of preliminary injunctions; required where permanent injunctions are postponed till final decrees; required where permanent injunctions are suspended pending appeals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bond/security is a recurring equitable device in patent injunction contexts with multiple specific uses (preliminary injunctions, appeals, postponement of permanent relief).

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof allocations in patent litigation — index items
rubrics_metrics.description: Burden of Proof: in suit to compel issue of letters patent; on questions of abandonment; on questions of damages; on questions of delay in applying for reissues; on questions of duration of patents; on questions of infringement; on questions of intention in qui tam cases; on questions of invention; on questions of novelty; on questions of profits; on questions of utility; on questions of validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index lists the allocation of burdens across many subspecialty patent questions; consult cited sections for specifics on which party bears each burden.
